info.title: CommonGrid API
info.description:
The CommonGrid open-source energy infrastructure API. Access data on utilities, grid operators, power plants, EV charging stations, transmission lines, pricing nodes, and more.

## Authentication

All endpoints are publicly accessible at the Anonymous tier (60 requests/hr, no per-minute burst). To unlock the Registered tier (5,000 requests/hr + 100/min burst), create a free API key in the [Developer Dashboard](/developers) and include it as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer cg_your_api_key
```

Only `Authorization: Bearer <key>` is accepted. Other `Authorization` schemes (e.g. `Basic`, a raw token without a scheme) return `401`. The `X-API-Key` header is unsupported and ignored — it does not authenticate or elevate rate limits.

Present-but-invalid credentials (unknown, revoked, or malformed Bearer tokens) also return `401`; they do not fall back to the anonymous tier. Missing credentials use the anonymous tier.

## Rate Limits

Authenticated read tiers check **both** a rolling hourly budget and a short burst window (whichever trips first returns `429`). Anonymous is hourly-only. Mutating requests use the write tier.

| Tier | Hourly | Burst | Auth Required |
|------|--------|-------|---------------|
| Anonymous | 60/hr | — | No |
| Registered | 5,000/hr | 100/min | API key |
| Bulk | 50,000/hr | 500/min | Contact us |
| Write | — | 100/min | Any mutating request |

Every limited response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, and `X-RateLimit-Tier` for the window that applied. On `429 RATE_LIMITED`, `Retry-After` is also set and matches that same window (burst rejections often show a short `Retry-After` and a burst-sized `X-RateLimit-Limit`).

## Pagination

List endpoints return cursor-based pagination:

```json
{
  "data": [...],
  "meta": {
    "total": 3000,
    "limit": 50,
    "nextCursor": "eyJ2IjoxLCJzIjp7InZhbHVlIjoiYWNtZS11dGlsaXR5In0sImlkIjoiYWJjMTIzIn0"
  }
}
```

Pass `cursor=<nextCursor>` to fetch the next page. Use the `limit` parameter (max 200) to control page size.

## Spec generation

This OpenAPI document is auto-generated from the Drizzle schema via `npm run generate:openapi`. CI verifies the committed spec is up to date on every PR; if you change a table or route and the spec diverges, `npm run check:openapi` will fail.

bearerAuth.description: API key obtained from the Developer Dashboard. Prefix with `cg_`. Only Bearer is accepted; `X-API-Key` and other Authorization schemes are not supported.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1–200, default 50)

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: Pagination cursor from the previous response `meta.nextCursor`

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to include in the response (sparse fieldsets)

slug.name: slug
slug.description: Unique URL-safe identifier for the resource

at.name: at
at.description: Point-in-time read. Reconstructs the entity from version history at the latest version with changed_at ≤ this instant. Accepts YYYY-MM-DD (end of that UTC day) or an ISO-8601 timestamp. Response includes `_as_of: { requested, versionNumber, changedAt }`. Returns 404 when no version exists at or before the requested time.

limit.description: Page size used for this response

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null if no more pages

ErrorResponse.description: Standard public API error envelope produced by `formatError`. All public `/api/v1` error responses use this shape (including geometry unknown-slug 404s).

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 time when the error was formatted.

details.description: Optional structured context (e.g. `{ "slug": "…" }` on geometry 404s, or validation field errors).

RateLimitedError.description: Returned when either the hourly or burst rate-limit window is exceeded. Header values describe the window that tripped.

message.example: Too many requests. Please slow down.

currentLimit.description: Budget of the window that was enforced (hourly or burst)

retryAfter.description: Seconds until X-RateLimit-Reset for the window that tripped

upgrade.description: Present on anonymous 429s — points callers at free API key registration

changeType.description: One of: create, update, delete, baseline

sourceType.description: Origin of this version: sync, community, admin, merge, or community_override

name.description: Free-form utility name. May also be a string containing '@domain' to trigger domain matching.

state.description: Optional two-letter US state code. Narrows candidates to utilities in that state.

domain.description: Optional email/web domain (e.g. 'duke-energy.com'). Combined with name when name does not already contain '@'.

confidence_threshold.description: Minimum trigram similarity (0..1) required to return a fuzzy match as the resolved utility. Defaults to 0.85.

eia_id.description: Resolved EIA utility id, or null when no match met the confidence threshold.

match_source.description: Which resolver phase produced the match.

canonical_name.description: Canonical utility name for the resolved id, when a match was found.

candidates.description: Up to 5 candidates considered, ordered by score desc. Populated even when no candidate met the threshold.

resolver_version.description: Semantic version of the resolver algorithm. Clients can pin this to detect algorithm changes.

UtilityGeometryFeatureCollection.description: GeoJSON FeatureCollection returned by `/utilities/{slug}/geometry`. Always 200 when the utility exists; `metadata.geometry_status` tells the caller whether the polygon is loaded or still pending backfill.

features.description: Zero or one `Feature<MultiPolygon>`. Empty when `metadata.geometry_status` is `pending_backfill`; contains one feature when `loaded`.

geometry_status.description: `loaded` when the territory polygon is available; `pending_backfill` when the utility exists in the registry but its polygon has not been ingested yet (known data gap).

source.description: Data source for the polygon (e.g. `HIFLD`, `EIA-861`). `null` when `geometry_status` is `pending_backfill`.

updated_at.description: When the territory row was last updated. Present on `loaded` responses.

SearchResults.description: Grouped search results keyed by entity type (camelCase plural).

get.description: Resolves a utility slug to its service-territory polygon and returns a GeoJSON `FeatureCollection` with a `metadata` block describing the resolved utility and `geometry_status`. Resolution follows utilities → regions (`SERVICE_TERRITORY`) → territories internally, so consumers only need the utility slug. Returns `200` with `features: []` and `metadata.geometry_status: "pending_backfill"` for utilities whose territory polygon has not been ingested yet (a known data gap that the backfill pipeline resolves over time) and `200` with one `Feature<MultiPolygon>` and `metadata.geometry_status: "loaded"` when geometry is available. Returns `404` with the standard `ErrorResponse` envelope (`code: "NOT_FOUND"`, `details.slug`) only when the slug is not in the registry. Responses are served as `application/geo+json` with cache headers that differentiate loaded (1h) from pending (5m).

post.summary: Resolve a utility name to an EIA id
post.description: Resolves a free-form utility name (optionally scoped by state or an email domain) to a canonical EIA utility id. Useful for researchers, journalists, and anyone joining an external dataset (news articles, complaint databases, email sign-ups) against the utility registry. Cascades through a manual override table, an exact normalized-name match, a domain match when the input looks like an email, and a trigram fuzzy match. Returns the resolved id plus the top 5 candidates considered.
